newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LONDON SIDE TO FACE F.A. CUP FINAL NEWCOMERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LONDON SIDE TO FACE F.A. CUP FINAL NEWCOMERS.

text.p: This season's English F.A. Cup final will be contested between one club from London and one which has never been in the final before following the semifinal draw made on Sunday.
The pairings for the last four mean Wimbledon will play Chelsea on April 13 while premier league Middlesbrough and second divison Chesterfield clash in the other semifinal on the same day.
The venues will be announced on Monday but could be Arsenal's north London ground Highbury and Hillsborough in Sheffield.
Chesterfield, Chelsea and Wimbledon all joined Middlesbrough in the last four on Sunday after their victories over Wrexham, Portsmouth and Sheffield Wednesday respectively.
Middlesbrough made sure of their place in the semifinals for the first time in their 121 year history when they beat fellow premier league rivals Derby 2-0 on Saturday.

Chesterfield, who have never achieved anything of note in their 131 year history, put that right when they defeated fellow second division rivals Wrexham 1-0 at home to become the first club from the third tier of English soccer to reach the semifinal stage for 13 years. Only six other teams from that level have gone that far but none of the previous six made it to the final.
Chelsea, who won their only F.A. Cup title in 1970 and lost the finals of 1915, 1967 and 1994, won through in convincing style, 4-1 at Portsmouth.

Wimbledon, who knocked out holders Manchester United in the fourth round, won 2-0 at Sheffield Wednesday in an uncompromising match that tipped Wimbledon's way late in the game after Wednesday had lost defender Jon Newsome and midfielder Graham Hyde with leg injuries during the first half. Neither are expected to play again this season.
Wimbledon's manager Joe Kinnear was a member of the Tottenham side that beat Chelsea in the 1967 Cup final.
He would like to score another cup victory over them this time as a manager and his side could yet be on their way to two finals this season.
Both the League and F.A. Cup finals could be between Wimbledon and Middlesbrough. Both look set to win their League Cup semifinal second legs over Leicester and Stockport respectively this week.

This season's F.A. Cup competition, with the big five -- Manchester United, Tottenham, Arsenal, Everton and Liverpool -- all going out relatively early, has been full of unlikely fairy tales and dramas with Chesterfield's arrival in the last four the most unlikely of them all.

Until this season, Chesterfield best ever performance in the cup were three fifth round appearances, the last of those 47 years ago when they beat Middlesbrough in the fourth round before losing to Chelsea in the fifth.

Now they stand just 90 minutes from Wembley after a deserved 1-0 win over Wrexham thanks to a second half goal from journeyman striker Chris Beaumont. The scenes at their modest Saltergate ground with thousands of fans celebrating on the pitch afterwards carrying their conquering heroes back to the dressing rooms reduced some disbelieving older fans to tears of joy.

Middlesbrough, who won at Derby on Saturday with goals from Brazilian Juninho and Italian Fabrizio Ravanelli remain in the dubious position of being on the verge of two finals as well as relegation from the premier league.

If they do get to the Cup final and play Chelsea there will be a distinct Latin flavour to the match with possibly four Italian players involved including Ravanelli and Chelsea's Gianluca Vialli, team mates in Juventus's European Cup success last season.

Wimbledon's Robbie Earle maintained his record of scoring in every round of this season's competition with the 75th minute opener against Wednesday with substitute Dean Holdsworth adding the second in the last minute.
The only time Wimbledon reached the semifinal was in 1988 when they went on to win the cup. The way they are playing at the moment that is an omen that cannot be discounted.
